issues.description: The template's PersonService declares a constructor that accepts a PersonRepository and assigns it to the final field (constructor injection), whereas the solution's PersonService provides a no-argument constructor that sets the repository field to null. This constructor parameter mismatch can confuse students about how the service is meant to receive its repository and will prevent proper repository usage (null repository) if adopted; it contradicts the intended constructor-based dependency injection shown in the template and described usage in the problem statement.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution's PersonService use the same constructor signature as the template (inject PersonRepository via constructor) and assign it to the repository field (or use proper @Autowired constructor injection). For example, change the no-arg constructor to public PersonService(PersonRepository personRepository) { this.personRepository = personRepository; } so behavior and dependency injection are consistent with the template and exercise description.
